requires: The source reference resolves to a committed revision in the current repository.
MH-C-ENV-001 is accepted and its dispatcher can describe every recorded profile.
Every supplied local or CI observation identifies its command, profile, platform, interpreter, status, and immutable output identity.
The destination is a repository-relative path that does not already exist.
ensures: The output is one canonical UTF-8 JSON artifact using schema mathhead.legacy-baseline.v1.

The artifact records source commit and tree identities, package and build metadata, tracked-source inventory, test collection, profile results, failure categories, CI run links, benchmark observations, known platform failures, and performance hot spots.
Every result distinguishes observed passed, failed, timed_out, unsupported, and not_run states without converting missing evidence into success.
Every external observation carries a stable provenance locator and every local file observation carries SHA-256 evidence.
Replay recomputes all source-derived fields and fails on source drift, malformed evidence, omitted required sections, unstable ordering, or hash mismatch.
Capture and replay leave product source, accepted contracts, PLAN, TODO, and existing PROGRESS history unchanged.
raises: Expected repository, schema, source-reference, evidence, subprocess, timeout, or destination failures return a nonzero status with a stable reason code.
No Python exception crosses the CLI boundary for an expected validation failure.
Programmer defects may produce a traceback only in explicit debug mode.

effects.filesystem: capture creates exactly one previously absent baseline artifact and tool-owned temporary files; replay is read-only except tool-owned caches
effects.process: may execute bounded git, package-metadata, dispatcher, test-collection, and benchmark inspection subprocesses
effects.network: none; remote CI evidence is supplied as immutable identifiers and links rather than fetched during capture or replay
effects.repository: never modifies product source, accepted contracts, PLAN, TODO, existing PROGRESS history, or the referenced source commit

determinism.serialization: UTF-8 JSON with sorted keys, stable separators, LF termination, and no absolute checkout paths
determinism.ordering: paths, tests, profiles, failures, CI observations, benchmarks, and hot spots use documented stable sort keys
determinism.time: wall-clock timestamps and raw durations are excluded from canonical identity; bounded performance observations use declared environment and threshold fields
determinism.source: all source-derived values are computed from the explicit committed source reference, never an implicit moving branch

budget.child_timeout: each subprocess has an explicit timeout no greater than the remaining operation budget
budget.cancellation: terminate the active child process and return a distinct interrupted result

epistemics.observed: the named command actually ran in the declared environment and its exit status plus output identity are present
epistemics.source_derived: the field is reproducibly computed from the committed source tree
epistemics.reported_external: the field cites an immutable CI run or job locator but is not re-executed by capture
epistemics.not_run: no qualifying observation was supplied; never equivalent to passed
epistemics.replayed: all source-derived fields and artifact invariants were recomputed successfully against the exact source reference

invariants: The baseline schema and required section names are stable within contract v1.
The baseline source commit is an ancestor of the capture commit and is never the mutable working-tree state.
Known failures and unsupported platforms remain first-class evidence and cannot be omitted to make the baseline green.
Test collection identities are unique and sorted; aggregate counts equal the categorized observations.
Every recorded path is repository-relative, exact-case, and free of parent traversal.
Replay never executes the legacy product test suite and therefore cannot silently replace captured outcomes with a later environment.
A baseline is not compatibility authority; it is an immutable differential oracle input governed by reconstruction ADRs.
